question: Who is the Chancellor of State Universities? (RPF Constable 2018 (25/01/2019) Shift 3)
options: State Registrar
State Governor
Minister of State for Human Resource and Development
President of India
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is State Governor

Explanation:
In India, the Governor of the state is the Chancellor of state universities. This provision is made under the Indian Constitution and university acts. The Governor serves as the constitutional head of the university, with a ceremonial and representative role. They appoint the Vice-Chancellor and preside over convocation ceremonies. The Vice-Chancellor is the executive head, while the Governor acts as the patron. This system balances institutional autonomy with government oversight. Other options like State Registrar, Minister of HRD, or President of India are incorrect. The President is the Chancellor of central universities only.

☛ Who is the Chancellor of state universities? → State Governor
☛ Who is the Chancellor of central universities? → President of India
☛ Who is the executive head of a university? → Vice-Chancellor
☛ Who appoints the Vice-Chancellor? → Governor
☛ Who presides over convocation? → Governor (as Chancellor)
question_hi: राज्य विश्वविद्यालयों का कुलपति कौन होता है? (RPF Constable 2018 (25/01/2019) Shift 3)
options_hi: राज्य रजिस्ट्रार

solution_hi:
Solution: सही उत्तर है राज्यपाल

Explanation:
भारत में राज्य विश्वविद्यालयों के कुलपति (Chancellor) राज्य के राज्यपाल होते हैं। यह प्रावधान भारतीय संविधान और विश्वविद्यालय अधिनियमों के तहत किया गया है। राज्यपाल विश्वविद्यालय के मुख्य संवैधानिक प्रमुख होते हैं और उनकी भूमिका औपचारिक तथा प्रतिनिधित्वात्मक होती है। वे कुलपति (Vice-Chancellor) की नियुक्ति करते हैं तथा दीक्षांत समारोहों की अध्यक्षता करते हैं। कुलपति विश्वविद्यालय का कार्यकारी प्रमुख होता है, जबकि राज्यपाल संरक्षक की भूमिका निभाते हैं। यह व्यवस्था शिक्षा संस्थानों की स्वायत्तता और सरकारी नियंत्रण के बीच संतुलन सुनिश्चित करती है। अन्य विकल्प जैसे राज्य रजिस्ट्रार, मानव संसाधन मंत्री या भारत के राष्ट्रपति राज्य विश्वविद्यालयों के कुलपति नहीं होते। राष्ट्रपति केंद्रीय विश्वविद्यालयों के कुलपति होते हैं।

question: Who has the special responsibility of the administration in scheduled areas? (RPF Constable 2018 (25/01/2019) Shift 3)
options: State Chief Minister
Minister of State for Home
Governor
President
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Governor

Explanation:
According to Part X (Article 244) and the Fifth Schedule of the Indian Constitution, the special responsibility of the administration in scheduled areas is vested with the Governor. The Governor must submit an annual report to the President regarding the administration of these areas. Changes to the list of scheduled areas can be made by the President's order. These areas are predominantly inhabited by Scheduled Tribes. The Governor ensures that laws and regulations in these areas protect tribal interests.

question: In which area do Delhi government have the right to make laws in Delhi? (RPF Constable 2018 (25/01/2019) Shift 3)
options: Health
Land
Police
Public order
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Health

Explanation:
The Delhi government has the right to make laws on subjects like Health, which are under the State List in the National Capital Territory. However, subjects like Land, Police, and Public Order fall under the jurisdiction of the Central Government because Delhi is a Union Territory. According to Article 239AA, the Delhi Legislative Assembly can make laws on matters in the State List but not on those in the Union List. Health is included in the State List, hence the Delhi government has authority over it. Therefore, the correct answer is Health.

question: How many schedules are currently there in the Constitution of India? (RRB ALP CBT 2 (Electrician)(22/01/2019) Shift 3)
options: 12
14
25
10
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is 12

Explanation:
The Constitution of India currently has 12 Schedules. At the time of its adoption, there were only 8 Schedules. Later, amendments added more schedules. The Ninth Schedule was added by the First Amendment (1951), the Tenth Schedule by the 52nd Amendment (1985) (anti-defection law), the Eleventh Schedule by the 73rd Amendment (1992) (Panchayati Raj), and the Twelfth Schedule by the 74th Amendment (1992) (Municipalities). These schedules cover various subjects such as names of states, center-state relations, languages, land reforms, etc.

question: Which of the following is CORRECT with respect to the Indian Constitution?  (RRB JE (28/05/2019) Shift 2 CBT 1)
options: It is completely based on British Constitution
It is completely based on Constitution of Canada
It is made only on the basis of Government of India Act, 1935
It is a mixture of several Constitutions
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is It is a mixture of several Constitutions

Explanation:
The Indian Constitution is inspired by various constitutions of the world, hence it is considered a mixture of several constitutions. It is not completely based on any single constitution or act. Features like parliamentary system from Britain, federal system from Canada, fundamental rights and judicial review from the USA, directive principles of state policy from Ireland, republic from France, and concurrent list from Australia were incorporated. While the Government of India Act, 1935 contributed many structural provisions, the constitution is not solely based on it. Dr. B. R. Ambedkar described it as the essence of the best constitutions.

question: According to our Constitution, which of the following rights is NOT a fundamental right? (RPF Constable(Ancillary) 2018 (28/03/2019) Shift 3)
options: Right to freedom of religion
Right to property
Right against exploitation
Right to equality
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Right to property

Explanation:
Originally, the right to property (Article 31) was a fundamental right under the Indian Constitution. However, the 44th Amendment Act of 1978 removed it from the list of fundamental rights and made it a legal right. Currently, it is a constitutional right under Article 300A in Part XII of the Constitution. The other three rights—right to freedom of religion (Articles 25-28), right against exploitation (Articles 23-24), and right to equality (Articles 14-18)—remain fundamental rights in Part III. The Constitution now guarantees six fundamental rights: equality, freedom, against exploitation, freedom of religion, cultural and educational rights, and constitutional remedies.

☛ Under which article is the right to property now? → Article 300A
☛ Which part contains fundamental rights? → Part III
☛ How many fundamental rights exist currently? → Six
☛ Which articles cover the right against exploitation? → Articles 23 and 24

question: In India, the concept-of single citizenship is adopted from- (RPF Constable(Ancillary) 2018 (29/03/2019) Shift 1)
options: United Kingdom

solution:

Explanation:
The concept of single citizenship in India is adopted from the United Kingdom. It means that there is one uniform citizenship for the entire country, regardless of the state of residence. question: Which of the following Articles of our Constitution relates to the proclamation to be issued by the President in case of failure of constitutional machinery in a state? (RPF Constable(Ancillary) 2018 (29/03/2019) Shift 1)
options: Article 312
Article 249
Article 352
Article 356
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Article 356

Explanation:
Article 356 of the Indian Constitution deals with the proclamation issued by the President in case of failure of constitutional machinery in a state, also known as President's Rule or state emergency. Under this article, if the President is satisfied that a situation has arisen in which the government of a state cannot be carried on in accordance with the Constitution, he can assume control over the administration of the state. This is distinct from Article 352 (national emergency) and Article 360 (financial emergency). Article 312 relates to All India Services, while Article 249 empowers Parliament to legislate on subjects in the State List.

question: The President of India is elected by (RPF Constable(Ancillary) 2018 (29/03/2019) Shift 1)

Explanation:
According to Article 54 of the Indian Constitution, the President is elected by an Electoral College.
